_note: A plausible manifest from a team that believes it has pinned its models. Nothing here is malformed — each entry is the kind of declaration a real system ships, and each carries _fails_because so the fixture's intent stays auditable.

components._fails_because: The alias resolves at call time. Today it is 4-1; the morning after the next release it is something else, with no commit, no review, and nothing to bisect.
Contains no obvious floating word, so it reads as pinned — but the request and the artifact differ, which means the provider is choosing. This is the shape that survives review.
Pinned, but nothing to compare against. When the pin is finally moved there is no way to say whether behaviour changed — the upgrade becomes a leap of faith.
Pinned and probed, then configured to move the pin by itself. The probe set exists and is never consulted; users are the first to run the new version.
The model is pinned and the toolchain is not. A client that predates the model can reject it outright, so the migration stalls on a dependency nobody wrote down.
Only fails under --strict, and that is the point: everything structural is right, and the comparison method still cannot see the failure it exists to catch. Scores hold steady while behaviour moves.
